consumer.targetLayer: public-plan coordination contract and repository-family template

classifications.notes: Adopt the requirement to name the destination before expanding decision work; AgentSwitchboard remains authoritative for public-plan behavior.

classifications.candidate: Decision tickets instead of speculative implementation slices
classifications.notes: Mapped onto existing public-plan tasks only while decision-frontier mode is active; execution is handed to the existing bounded execution path.

classifications.candidate: Frontier, blocking, claim, fog-of-war, and destination out-of-scope semantics
classifications.notes: Frontier is derived from existing task status/dependencies/owner. Only fog and destination-scope exclusions gain structured fields, preventing a duplicate frontier store.

classifications.candidate: Map-as-index and one canonical decision owner
classifications.notes: Decision details remain owned by the public-plan task and its evidence pointers; summaries may gist but may not fork the decision.

classifications.candidate: Wayfinder issue labels, child-issue representation, native tracker blocking, and local-markdown fallback
classifications.notes: Tracker mechanics remain donor-specific. AgentSwitchboard uses its existing plan/task/dependency contract and does not import a second tracker model.
Those skill names and their HITL/AFK conventions belong to the donor ecosystem and must not be reimplemented as AgentSwitchboard authority.

classifications.candidate: Pinned-source adoption metadata and stale-reference policy
classifications.notes: AgentSwitchboard records donor commit/path/blob authority and requires explicit reviewed refresh instead of silently following upstream main.

capabilitiesDonated: Name a destination before expanding a large ambiguous plan.
Represent unresolved work as decision questions rather than premature implementation slices.
Derive a takeable frontier from dependency and claim state instead of storing a second mutable frontier list.
Keep not-yet-specifiable in-scope fog separate from destination-level out-of-scope work.
Hand off to bounded execution when planning has made the route clear.
proofCeiling: This contribution proves only the pinned donor reference, AgentSwitchboard semantic mapping, closed consumer schema shape, template propagation, and offline consumer validators. It does not prove donor runtime behavior, issue-tracker child/dependency APIs, agent judgment quality, successful decision resolution, child-repository adoption, or any execution/merge/deployment outcome outside the consumer PR.
mustNotCopyOrReimplement: Do not copy the donor Wayfinder skill wholesale into AgentSwitchboard.
Do not create a second AgentSwitchboard wayfinder skill that competes with public-plan-coordination.
Do not import donor-specific issue labels, child-issue APIs, local tracker fallback, or skill invocation names as canonical AgentSwitchboard behavior.
Do not make child repositories depend directly on mattpocock/skills; they consume AgentSwitchboard's repository-family template when they adopt this mode.
Do not auto-update the donor commit when upstream main advances.
